activity_context.topic_title: Calculating the Eigenvectors of a 3x3 Matrix in the General Case

feedback.problem:
$$
G=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 5 & -1 \\ 0 & -3 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $G$ shown above. Which of the following is a basis of the eigenspace corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-3?$
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(G-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =-3.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}G-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 5 & -1 \\ 0 & -3 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}]-(-3)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}5{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=0 \\ -{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that its augmented matrix $M$ is already in row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $2$nd and the $3$rd). Thus, ${x}_{1}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{3}=0.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get ${x}_{2}=0.$ 

So, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]={x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{1}\in R.
$$

Therefore, the required basis is 

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}.
$$
